title: Unit – 5 : Session – 6 : SLO – 2  |  ARM Thumb Instruction Set
sections: 1. b) To reduce code size and memory usage.
3. c) They provide improved code density for memory-constrained systems.
4. a) By setting a bit in the CPSR (the T bit, changed via BX/BLX instructions).
3. TRUE — the CPSR T bit selects the instruction set state.
4. FALSE — NEON SIMD operations need ARM/NEON state, not Thumb.
1. Use Thumb: 16-bit instructions cut code size roughly in half versus 32-bit ARM code, so the control logic plus lookup tables fit the 64 KB flash with room for features.
2. Switching: via the CPSR T bit — executing BX/BLX with the target address bit-0 set enters Thumb state; clearing it returns to ARM state.

3. Trade-off: Thumb has a reduced instruction set — some operations need multiple Thumb instructions where one ARM instruction suffices, so performance-critical inner loops may run slower; typical practice is Thumb for bulk code, ARM state for hot paths.
